source: .github/workflows/ci.yml, job `test`, transcribed by reading the repository
constructedIndependently: Written by reading the workflow file. The inference engine was not consulted and this file is not generated from any ExecutionGraph.
cellSelection: Base matrix is os x node-version x babel-version x webpack-version = 2 x 2 x 2 x 1 = 8 cells, plus 4 `include` rows. The in-environment cell is (ubuntu-latest, 22, 7, 5), matching the CI ground-truth job name. Every windows-latest cell and every non-22 node version is OUT_OF_ENVIRONMENT, recorded and not executed.
conditionsApplied: The `Downgrade to Babel 7` step is gated on `matrix.babel-version == '7'`, which is TRUE for this cell, so it IS included. No other step declares an `if:`.
expressionsApplied: `matrix.webpack-version` is DEFINED('5') and `matrix.babel-version` is DEFINED('7'), so `yarn add -D webpack@${{ matrix.webpack-version }}` renders `webpack@5`. Unlike html-webpack-plugin's UNDEFINED_CONTEXT case, both axes here are genuinely declared.
shellBoundaryNote: `yarn up @babel/*@^7` carries `*` and `^`, both in SHELL_METACHARACTERS. Per docs/ci-reproduction-sample-01-amendment-5.md it is spawned with NO SHELL rather than rejected or shelled: the glob is not shell syntax here - bash would find no match, pass the string through untouched, and yarn expands it itself. The receipt records spawnedWithoutShell on that step.

steps.evidence: ENVIRONMENT, not a workflow command. Permitted by docs/ci-reproduction-sample-01-amendment-2.md: corepack ships with node 22, only creates shims, and is recorded as an explicit environment step.
.github/workflows/ci.yml - `Install webpack ${{ matrix.webpack-version }}` -> `run: yarn add -D webpack@${{ matrix.webpack-version }}`, with matrix.webpack-version DEFINED('5')
.github/workflows/ci.yml - `Downgrade to Babel 7` -> `run: yarn up @babel/*@^7`, gated on `if: matrix.babel-version == '7'` which is TRUE for this cell
.github/workflows/ci.yml - `Run tests for webpack version ${{ matrix.webpack-version }}` -> `run: yarn test-only`

notes: Single job, no cross-job artifact dependency, no third-party action wrapping the test command, no compound run: line, and no reference deviation. This is the cleanest pipeline in the sample and the only remaining candidate for a pristine REPRODUCED.
